title: Design a model
summary: Describe a database table with a Django model: fields, defaults, ordering and methods.
hints: Every new field is one line inside Book, lined up with title. For example author = models.CharField(max_length=100).
An optional number needs both options: null=True (the database may store no value) and blank=True (input checks allow it to be empty).
default=True sets is_available when nobody gives a value. auto_now_add=True makes Django fill in created_at by itself when the book is first saved.
Default ordering goes in a small class inside Book: a line class Meta:, then indented under it ordering = ['title'] (a list, with square brackets).
Methods take self: def is_classic(self):, and use self.published_year inside. None < 1950 crashes, so check self.published_year is not None and ... first.

quiz.question: What does null=True on a model field control?
options: Whether forms allow an empty value
Whether the database column can store NULL
Whether the field has a default
quiz.explanation: null is about the database. blank is about validation in forms and serializers. Optional non-text fields usually need both.

quiz.question: You added a field to a model. What must happen before the database has the new column?
options: Nothing, Django adds it on the fly
quiz.explanation: makemigrations writes a migration file that describes the change. migrate applies it to the database.

quiz.question: Why define __str__ on a model?
options: It controls how the object appears in the admin, shell and logs
It's used as the primary key
quiz.explanation: Without it you'll see Book object (1) everywhere. A readable __str__ makes the admin and debugging much nicer.
